entities.summary:
Wen Hu (died 291 CE), courtesy name Zhongruo, was a Chinese military general and politician who served the state of Cao Wei during the tumultuous Three Kingdoms period, and later the Jin dynasty. Son of the prominent general Wen Qin, Wen Hu inherited a legacy of military prowess and political entanglement, becoming a key participant in the mid-3rd century struggles that ultimately saw the Sima clan usurp the Cao Wei throne. His career unfolded amidst the escalating power vacuum following Cao Rui's death, marked by the regency of Cao Shuang and the subsequent rise of Sima Yi, which set the stage for decades of internecine conflict.

Wen Hu's most significant military actions occurred during the series of rebellions against the Sima regency, particularly the second Shouchun rebellion in 255 CE. Alongside his father Wen Qin and the general Guanqiu Jian, he led forces in an attempt to curb the burgeoning power of Sima Shi, then regent for Emperor Cao Mao. Though initially successful in rallying support, the rebellion was brutally suppressed, leading to his father's execution by Sun Chen of Eastern Wu after a desperate defection. Wen Hu, however, managed to escape to Eastern Wu, where he continued to serve until the state's conquest by the Jin dynasty in 280 CE.

After the fall of Eastern Wu, Wen Hu returned to the unified Jin dynasty, ironically serving the very Sima clan he had once vehemently opposed. His survival and subsequent integration into the Jin bureaucracy highlight the complex political pragmatism of the era, where former adversaries often found new roles in consolidated empires. His later life saw him serve in various capacities, including as an official in the Ministry of Works, demonstrating a remarkable adaptability and resilience in navigating the shifting political landscapes of post-Three Kingdoms China. His story exemplifies the challenges faced by hereditary military elites during periods of dynastic transition.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Wen Hu was a notable figure in the mid-3rd century power struggles, particularly his involvement in the Shouchun rebellions, which were pivotal in the Sima clan's rise to power and the eventual establishment of the Jin dynasty. His career reflects the broader political and military transitions of the Three Kingdoms era.
